title: "Chapter 4 — The God's Demand"
subtitle: "GM guide — Chapter 4"
---

*Vindolanda has endured six days of siege. Three simultaneous crises force triage while Mars demands the spear be carried below by nightfall. The party must survive the siege, navigate Roman politics, escort the spear through haunted tunnels, and kneel before a god.*

**Level:** 6 → Advance to 7 at session end · **Players:** 6 (Iris, Julia Jana, Tanit, Rivia, Ursula, Brian) · **Time:** 3–4 hrs · **Type:** Siege + Politics + Dungeon Escort

**What happened last session:**

- The grove ritual either succeeded (spear in Thusnelda's sealed clay jar) or failed (whole spear in hand)
- Vercingetorix is either an ally with a truce line or a neutral threat
- Cassia either gathered bog valerian (Siege Ward available) or didn't

- They advance to Level 6 at the start of this session

**What players currently believe:**

- The fort is under siege (they knew this was coming from Session 3's transition note)
- Mars was acknowledged but not fully satisfied
- They may not know Brutus launched the siege specifically to stop them

**What they don't know yet:**

- Corvinus already filed a report blaming them
- Lucius is still receiving ravens ordering Cassia's death
- Cassia will volunteer to kneel alone if no one else does
- Brutus does not know the ritual succeeded in Session 3 (his intelligence ends at the treeline)

**Open threads coming in:**

- What does "Mars demands witnesses" actually mean in practice?
- Can Corvinus be neutralized without violence?

<details>
<summary>📁 The Truth Behind the Session</summary>

**What is actually going on:**

Senator Brutus launched the siege when his agents reported the party had left the fort with the spear. He does not know about the grove ritual. He believes the spear can still be retrieved. Two Germanic chieftains in the warband owe him money and old favors — they organized the siege. Vercingetorix does not know this; if he did, it would reframe his alliance entirely.

Mars has given until nightfall. He will not destroy the fort if the spear reaches the antechamber on time. He is angry, not irrational. The party has done things he respects. He has been watching.

Corvinus is scared. He blames the party in his official report because having them as a controllable scapegoat is safer than admitting he doesn't understand what happened at this fort over the last month.

**NPC schedules — what happens if players do nothing:**

- Three crises play out: gate holds (barely), granary takes partial damage, shrine agent succeeds and steals the spear case (adding +2 to all Mars DCs later)
- Varro organizes triage without the party — effective, but slow
- Cassia emerges, speaks, waits for the party to lead
- Corvinus calls a council in the *principia* at midday whether or not anyone asks

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 0: Cold Open — The Bell and the Breach</summary>

**Read aloud immediately — no preamble:**

> *You are already running when the bell rings. Smoke pours from the west workshops. The north gate creaks, splinters, and finally gives. A Germanic battering ram lurches through the gap. Varro shouts for shields to form. Cassia staggers out of the shrine with fresh blood down her chin.*
>
> *"He demands the spear," she says. "If we do not take it below by nightfall he will feed the fort to his wolves."*

**Three simultaneous crises — party must triage. They engage two. The third resolves by NPC competence.**

| Crisis | Mechanics | Stakes if unengaged |
|---|---|---|
| Gate breach | Athletics DC 14 (active: holding the ram 3 rounds while engineers wedge beams). Failure: 1d4 soldiers lost, constant harassment during escort. | Off-screen: Varro holds it for 2 rounds. Engineers arrive late. 2 soldiers lost. |
| Granary fire | Survival DC 15 (active: firefighting each round) or Create Water. Each failed round: –1d6 rations. | Off-screen: Auxiliaries slow it. Rations –3 from stock. Food clock at 2. |
| Shrine desecration | Insight DC 14 (active: watching the shrine during chaos) to spot agent; contested Dex vs. +4 to intercept. If he escapes: Mars adds +2 to all DCs during Scenes 3–4. | Off-screen: succeeds. Handout 8 evidence still findable in the watchtower. |

**Reading the assault pattern:**

Perception DC 12 (active: from the wall before engaging any crisis): the north gate attack is the feint. The fire plume goes the wrong direction for an external fire. The real threat is the shrine. A character who calls this out gives the party advance warning — they can cover all three crises optimally.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 1: Council in the Principia</summary>

**Participants:** Corvinus, Lucius, Varro, Cassia, the party, Vercingetorix by runner.

**What each faction wants:**

| Faction | Position | What they'll trade |
|---|---|---|
| Corvinus | Roman Authority: his bodyguard escorts the spear. He arrests anyone refusing. | Extra legionaries ×4 — but he controls the route and the report. |
| Lucius | Secret Transfer: destroy the spear in the tunnels. "Controlled detonation." | He does not say what he's actually planning. Deception DC 14 to notice he's lying about the reason. |
| Varro | Shared Custody: three witnesses kneel with Cassia. Civilians in the procession. | Advantage on Mars interactions; weakens escort numbers. |
| Cassia | Three volunteers must kneel: one Roman, one Germanic, one tied to the spear. | She will not negotiate this requirement — Mars stated it. |
| Vercingetorix (runner) | Party swears to return the spear to the grove after the ritual. | His warriors stage the diversion, guard the fort overnight (long rest before Ch5). |

**The meaningful decision:** Choose or craft a hybrid:

1. **Roman Authority (Corvinus):** +4 legionaries; disadvantage on Persuasion with Vercingetorix.
2. **Shared Custody (Varro + Cassia):** Three kneeling witnesses chosen. Advantage on Mars checks; fewer escort soldiers.
3. **Secret Transfer (Lucius):** Betrayal path. The ritual fails. Mars is not deceived. See Ch5 complications.

**Reading the room:**

- Insight DC 13 (active: watching Corvinus while Cassia speaks): He is assembling arguments, not listening. His hand signs to his bodyguard captain are visible. On 5 above: he already has a contingency that does not include the party.
- Intimidation DC 14 (active: addressing Corvinus' bodyguard captain directly, invoking the party's four-session track record): On success, captain privately recommends deference. Corvinus accepts Shared Custody instead of pushing Roman Authority — but he does not thank anyone for it.
- Deception DC 14 (active: telling the bodyguard captain the tunnel route is already secured by Varro's standing orders): Buys time. Requires a document or a high-ranking speaker. Failure: captain reports the attempt immediately.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 2: Preparing the Procession</summary>

**Give Handout 9 here.** Players plan the escort on the Order of Battle sheet.

Allow up to three preparation actions:

| Preparation | Check | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Scout the hidden stair | Perception DC 14 (active: slow sweep of *principia* basement) | Finds pressure-plate trap (Thieves' Tools DC 13 to disarm). History DC 14 (passive): pre-Hadrianic design — fort built over an older installation. |
| Secure the vicus | Persuasion DC 15 (calming civilians) or Deception DC 14 (claiming routine supply transfer) | Prevents civilian panic during escort. Deception creates confusion when Mars' arrival becomes obvious. |
| Blessings | Religion DC 14 or Performance DC 14 (Cassia leads, or a PC leads as ceremony) | +1d4 temp HP to escort. |
| Calm the horses | Animal Handling DC 11 (before procession — horses react to spear proximity) | Failure: procession starts 10 minutes late; Corvinus notes it. |
| Map the tunnel gas | Nature DC 13 (passive, if entering tunnel entrance during scouting) | Air smells of marsh gas, not volcanic. Actionable in the Choking Hall: gas is denser near the floor, not the ceiling. Search for air pockets near ceiling. |

Each failed preparation check introduces one tunnel complication (collapsed passage, frightened auxiliary, etc.).

**Shadow-cursed PC moment (if present):** During preparation, if they step away from the group or look toward the south:

> *Your shadow stretches. Not with the torchlight — against it. It extends southward, toward the trees, like a hand reaching for something it recognizes. It stops at full extension and waits.*

Player choice: follow (toward Vercingetorix's camp), resist (Wisdom DC 12 or the shadow takes a full round to retract), or watch. The shadow retracts before anyone else notices. Trigger the Shadar-kai fading mechanic reset now.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 2b: The Testudo Floor Lock (Puzzle)</summary>

Found only if the party scouted the hidden stair (Perception DC 14 during Scene 2 preparation). If not scouted, the party enters Room 1 via a side passage — no puzzle, no risk, no chalk-mark connection.

**Setup:** Nine flagstones in a 3×3 grid block the base of the stair. Each stone is carved with a Roman soldier figure in a different posture: kneeling shield-bearer, standing pilum-thrower, crouching spear-braced, and six others. Stepping on a wrong stone triggers a retractable floor spike (2d4 piercing) and a creak loud enough to draw the Animated Armors in Room 1 toward the noise.

**The safe path:** Three stones only, matching the testudo formation's front rank foot positions: front-left then front-center then shield-right corner. An L-shape across the bottom and right edge of the grid.

**Clues available:**

| Clue | Source | What it reveals |
|---|---|---|
| Chalk marks on safe stones | Perception DC 12 (active: hold torch low, crouch to floor level) | Three faint chalk marks on the correct stones — someone used this route before |
| Formation pattern | History DC 14 (active: studying the carvings) | Soldier figures depict testudo front rank positions — a military formation puzzle |
| Handout 9 margin diagram | Active: party reads H9 carefully and studies the formation diagram | Small diagram in the margin shows shield-bearer foot positions — matches the three safe stones exactly |

**Mechanics:**

| Action | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Step on wrong stone | None — automatic | 2d4 piercing + loud creak (Perception DC 12 for anyone in Room 1 above) |
| Disarm triggered tile | Thieves' Tools DC 13 (active: crouching, exposed) | Resets one tile. Two tiles adjacent to correct path are unstable if not reset. |
| Carry the spear through | Athletics DC 11 (active: managing weight and balance on the three specific tiles) | Failure: stumble into an adjacent tile |
| Find the keystone bypass | Arcana DC 16 (active: studying the mechanism for one full minute) | A carved keystone in the wall resets all nine stones to safe. Takes one full round. Requires a free hand. |

**Hidden reward:** The chalk marks use the same handwriting as the wax tablet from the Session 1 vault. A character who saw that tablet and succeeds on History DC 14 (passive) makes the connection — someone used this route before the fort was built. Do not explain it. Leave it as a world detail.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 3: The Procession Below</summary>

**Read aloud when the stair opens:**

> *The flagstones of the principia grind apart. Cold damp air rises carrying the smell of old blood and iron. Torches gutter sideways even though there is no wind. The spear pulses once with a deep red glow. Mars has opened the way.*

Three consecutive tunnel rooms. At each: who leads, who guards civilians, who carries the spear? Those choices affect Session 5 corruption checks.

**Room 1 — The Sunken Armory:**

Fallen Roman armor pieces animate when touched by spear-light. 4 Animated Armors (constructs — no Turn Undead, no undead vulnerabilities).

- Perception DC 11 (active, before spear-light reaches the room): pieces are in formation — two files, advance rank, reserve rank behind a pillar. A soldier who calls this out: first defender following the layout has advantage on their first attack.
- History DC 14 (passive): pre-Hadrianic armor, 80–100 years older than the fort. Sealed when Vindolanda was built over it.
- Arcana DC 14 (passive): divine resonance — consecrated legionary armor responding to the spear's light.
- Clue under a corroded shield: Latin inscription *"The god hears the loudest heart."*

**Room 2 — The Choking Hall:**

Poisonous gas vents. Constitution DC 14 (active: each round in the hall) unless using the rune map to find air pockets, or Cassia spends a spell slot to clear it.

- If gas mapped during preparation (Nature DC 13): gas is denser near the floor. Air pockets are near the ceiling. Stealth DC 13 (active: moving slow and high to locate pockets by feel) gives advantage on Con saves.
- Medicine DC 13 (active: treating an unconscious party member): stabilizes without spending a spell slot.

**Room 3 — The Elder Stair:**

Narrow steps around a dry well. Brutus' agent triggers a rockfall attempting to bury the spear.

- Dexterity save DC 15 (active: reacting) or Acrobatics DC 13 (active: bracing against the wall) — use whichever the player declares first.
- Failure: 2d8 bludgeoning and the spear slides toward the shaft. Contested Strength check to keep it.
- Agent is caught here or escapes into the tunnels. Either way: Ch5 opening reflects the outcome.

**Three Kneeling Figures:**

At the final door, Mars demands three mortals kneel in submission. Cassia insists: one Roman, one Germanic, one tied to the spear.

If the party refuses: Mars adds an extra trial in Session 5 (one additional animated stone golem in the confrontation).

</details>

---

<details>
<summary>📁 Scene 4: The Antechamber of Mars</summary>

**Read aloud:**

> *The chamber beyond is circular, carved before Rome existed. The air hums like taut bowstrings. In the center stands the same granite altar where the spear once rested. Above it hangs a vision of Vindolanda seen from the clouds: burning, flooded, broken. Mars' voice vibrates in your bones rather than your ears.*
>
> *"Bring me what is mine and speak your price."*

**The callback:** This is the same chamber as Session 1. The same altar, the same chain anchors, the Wight's remains if the party left them. The campaign begins and ends in the same circle of stone. Narrate the recognition explicitly.

**The door does not open immediately.** Three Latin words are carved above the lintel: *AUDIT DEUS COR* — "The god hears the heart." Below them, in Elder Futhark: ANSUZ (ᚨ), THURISAZ (ᚦ), WUNJO (ᚹ). Cassia translates quietly: *"He is asking for something true."* This is the answer to the Room 1 clue ("The god hears the loudest heart"). If the party found it, make the connection explicit.

**The Riddle of the Loudest Heart:**

Each of the three kneeling mortals must answer aloud, in their own words: *"What have you given for this mission that you cannot take back?"*

Mars will not open the chamber until all three have spoken. The honesty of the answer matters. The eloquence does not. Insight DC 12 (passive, any witness): detects a hollow or deflected answer before the inscription reacts — lets other party members redirect the speaker privately.

| Answer type | What happens |
|---|---|
| True cost stated in character | Inscription dims. Waits for remaining speakers. |
| Deflected or hollow answer | Inscription glows red once. Speaker may try again. Second deflection: 1d6 psychic damage. |
| Silent refusal | 1d4 psychic damage per round of silence. The inscription does not repeat the question. It waits. |
| One character answers for all three | Inscription glows red. The word *COR* — heart — returns alone. Each must speak. |

After all three have spoken: the carving darkens, the lintel drops inward, the chamber opens with a breath of cold air. No roll required. Only truth.

**Payoff:** Any kneeling character who gave a genuine answer at the door has their HP cost at the sacrifice altar reduced by 5 HP (minimum 5 HP). Mars heard them before they knelt.

**The sacrifice declaration:**

| Offer | Effect |
|---|---|
| Blood: 10 HP per kneeling volunteer | Mars accepts. One corruption stage removed per chosen character. |
| Glory: swear to bear the blame for what follows | Advantage on Persuasion vs. legionaries in Ch5; they become the scapegoat if things go poorly. |
| Obedience: promise to answer Mars' Call to War (Ch5 mechanic) | Favorable Ch5 start. Obligates them. Mars tracks promises. |

After the offering, the spear levitates to the altar. Mars speaks: *"Tomorrow you stand before me."*

Cut immediately to the fort above. The siege pauses. Germanic horns fall silent. Every NPC knows something profound just occurred.

</details>
